annotations.text:
Volume belongs to the task, not the phone.
Every alarm keeps its own level, as a share of the Ringer & Alerts volume iOS rings alarms at. Dragging a slider or previewing a tone plays the very sound the alarm will ring with, at that same volume — what you hear is what wakes you. Swipe left on a row to delete.

Editing an alarm.
New alarms open on the current time, carrying the volume, sound, snooze, fade-in and vibration of the last alarm saved. Saving switches an alarm on. Fade-in starts off; switched on, it ramps over 10 s. Vibrate buzzes while the alarm rings in the app; on the Lock Screen, iOS's Haptics setting decides. Dragging the slider plays the alarm's own sound at the Ringer & Alerts volume; with the Silent switch on it is muted, and a line under the slider says so (not drawn here). The editor scrolls — this artboard is taller to show all of it.

Picking a sound.
The fade-in curve appears only when fade-in is on. iOS does not share its own tone library with apps, so the choices are the bundled tones and your own audio from Music or Files.

Ringing in the app.
A small Snooze, and Stop as a slide so a stray tap cannot silence the alarm. On the Lock Screen, iOS draws the ringing alarm itself; apps only set its button text, icon and colour.

Snoozed, on the Lock Screen.
The dark card is the app's Live Activity counting down to when the alarm returns; it keeps the same colours in both themes. The notice below it is posted the moment you snooze, so a snooze is never invisible.

Sounds and Settings.
Sounds auditions any tone at any level — drag to hear it live, exactly as it will ring. Settings holds the clock, what happens when an alarm rings, and the theme. New-alarm defaults are learned from saved alarms rather than set here, and on iOS 26 every alarm rings through Silent, so the Override Silent switch is gone.

Light
When the phone is in light mode. Appearance is Auto on first launch, so the app follows the phone — as does the clock, which starts on Match device. Warm paper neutrals; amber deepens for text and icons so it holds contrast on white.

Dark
When the phone is in dark mode. Same layout; either theme can be pinned in Settings › Appearance.
